questions.q: What is the `system` catalog, and how is it billed?
options: A built-in Unity Catalog catalog holding an account's operational data; it's free to query, you only pay for the compute used
A paid add-on catalog that must be purchased separately from Unity Catalog
A temporary catalog that is deleted and regenerated every 24 hours
A catalog that only account owners, never admins, can access
questions.explain: System tables are read-only and free to query; the only cost is the compute resource used to run the query against them, exactly like any other catalog.

questions.q: Does an account admin need an explicit GRANT to query system tables?
options: No — account and metastore admins have access by default; every other user needs an explicit grant
Yes — even admins must be granted USE CATALOG on system manually
No one can ever grant access to system tables
Only workspace admins (not account admins) have default access
questions.explain: Account and metastore admins get system table access by default; other users need USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA, and SELECT grants, the same pattern as any other catalog.

questions.q: Which schema in the system catalog holds billing usage and SKU pricing history?
options: system.billing
system.access
system.compute
system.lakeflow
questions.explain: system.billing holds tables like system.billing.usage (all billable usage) and system.billing.list_prices (historical SKU pricing).

questions.q: What happens if you run an unfiltered, highly non-selective query against a large system table?
options: It's rejected with an error asking for a more selective query, rather than just running slowly
It silently returns zero rows
It automatically adds a LIMIT 1000 to the query
It queues the query for off-peak execution
questions.explain: To prevent performance issues, Databricks returns a 'System Table query returned too much data' error for queries that aren't sufficiently selective — filtering on a date column is the usual fix.

questions.q: Why should a job that reads a system table be built to tolerate schema evolution?
options: New columns can be added to system tables at any time without notice
System table schemas are rewritten from scratch every week
System tables have no fixed schema at all
Databricks deprecates old system tables every quarter
questions.explain: Existing columns won't change or be removed, but new columns may be added at any time — a job relying on a fixed schema can break unless it tolerates or enables schema evolution.
